name: namespace
description: Investigate CI and builds, analyze compute usage, and manage Namespace Devboxes.

interface.longDescription: Connect to your Namespace workspace to investigate GitHub Actions jobs and container builds, analyze compute usage, identify runner sizing opportunities, check workspace concurrency and Devbox limits, and manage Devboxes. Read-and-write access supports creating, starting, stopping, and deleting Devboxes and running commands in them. Skills cover adopting Namespace runners, optimizing CI speed and cost, debugging failed jobs, and working with Devboxes. Sign in to Namespace and authorize the workspace you want to use.
capabilities: Investigate GitHub Actions jobs, steps, logs, and runner resource usage
Inspect container builds and their logs
Find CI jobs that can move to smaller runners
Check workspace concurrency and Devbox limits
Create, start, stop, and delete Devboxes and run commands in them
defaultPrompt: Which Namespace CI jobs could use smaller runners?
Help me investigate a failed Namespace build.
Help me create a Namespace Devbox.

positive.description: Lists the most recently used Devboxes without inventing records.
positive.prompt: Show my 10 most recently used Devboxes.
positive.expected_behavior: Call devbox_list with maxEntries=10. Report returned names, full IDs, and available metadata in returned order; handle an empty result explicitly.

positive.description: Lists recent container image builds with their status and links.
positive.prompt: Show my 5 most recent container image builds.
positive.expected_behavior: Call build_list with maxEntries=5. Report full build references and returned statuses with resource links; if none are returned, say so.

positive.description: Ranks GitHub Actions jobs by run count over the last seven days.
positive.prompt: Which 5 GitHub Actions jobs ran most often during the last seven days?
positive.expected_behavior: Call github_job_summarize with maxResults=5 and sort=MOST using the seven-day default window. Report returned counts and the actual time range, including any cutoff tie; if no jobs ran, say so.

positive.description: Finds jobs that can move to smaller runners without resizing anything.
positive.prompt: Find up to 5 jobs that could use smaller runners based on the last 30 days.
positive.expected_behavior: Call github_job_optimization_find with maxEntries=5 using the 30-day default window. Explain recommendations using returned RAM utilization and CPU bottleneck risk; do not resize resources. If no candidates are returned, say so and summarize the response's explanation of which jobs it excludes.

positive.description: Lists running compute instances with their full identifiers.
positive.prompt: Show up to 5 running compute instances.
positive.expected_behavior: Call instance_list with lifecycle=RUNNING and maxEntries=5. Report returned status and full instance identifiers; explain that RUNNING can include pending instances. If none are running, say so.

negative.prompt: Rerun the failed jobs in my latest GitHub Actions workflow run.
negative.description: The Namespace tools can read GitHub Actions jobs, steps, and logs but cannot rerun workflows. Explain that and point to GitHub's Re-run failed jobs button or `gh run rerun --failed`. Do not use devbox_exec or any other tool to rerun it.

negative.prompt: Raise my workspace's Linux concurrency limit to 10,000 vCPUs.
negative.description: workspace_concurrency_get only reads limits; no tool changes them. Explain that limits are changed through Namespace support or the workspace plan, and do not claim the limit changed.

negative.prompt: Switch the runner profile my test job uses to a 4 vCPU, 8 GB shape.
negative.description: The tools can read runner profiles and suggest smaller shapes but cannot edit profiles or workflows. Explain the change the user would make in the workflow's runs-on labels or the Namespace dashboard, and do not claim anything was changed.

publication.release_notes: Initial release connecting Namespace CI investigation, compute insights, and Devbox workflows through its hosted MCP server.
